dehydrated_text:
This is now empire, guys. So, Pericles should be embarking on a massive war of expansion against Sparta but doesn't because he avoids fighting them. By forcing everyone to seek shelter within Athens, where Sparta is a land power, Pericles ensures they don't face each other on land. Placing many people in one place leads to disease.

Guess what happens if you put a lot of people in one place? You get the plague, guys. This kills a third of the Athenian population, including Pericles and his two sons.

Can you read this? The different islands are either rebelling against Athens or requesting not to be part of their war. Athenians respond by saying they will not trouble you with pretenses about having a right to their empire because they overthrew Persia or attacked you for wrongs done. Instead, they aim at what is feasible, holding the view that right in the world is only between equals, where the strong do as they can and the weak suffer what they must.

Remember how Persians offered friendship with the idea of not defeating them but simply being friends. The Athenians are even worse; after defeating Persia, they claim their empire and demand obedience without trying to be friends or convincing others that they are right.

The war drags on because as an empire, Athens becomes lazy, stupid, and arrogant, leading them to invade Sicily, a people not part of the war. Athenians collect tribute from allies but need more money during this prolonged conflict, so they decide to conquer Syracuse with its navy and drag it into the war.

Now Sparta and Syracuse combine against Athens, and Persians join as well. Allies turn against Athens, blockading them in Attica where most wheat comes from. Athens starves and surrenders, ending the Peloponnesian War. Spartans could choose to destroy Athens but don't because they only want to maintain the status quo equilibrium.

This gives rise to Macedonia, which will later learn the major innovations of both Athenians and Spartans.
